turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: In La Paz this week the city pays its year-end bonus early. 71.5m pesos, on the twelfth of November.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Without a loan.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Mayor Quiroga says the money comes from their own revenue, after some property taxes arrived ahead of time at a discount.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Mm.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The portal tracks 8,993 housing actions financed for 6,560 million pesos.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What happens when those numbers start to drift apart from what people earn?

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: This is Radio BCS2050. Today a deep dive on Finance, and the question we chase is how a city pays its way when the usual sources thin.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Meganoticias reports that FEDECOOP and the state presented Shell Nurse artificial reefs in La Paz Bay at the Sea of Cortez Forum.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: A response to warmer water for the fishers.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The bay still holds morning light on the water when the fishers head out. Yes. Secihti funds the study, and the IDB runs the cost-benefit numbers. Next they protect the sites and check if it spreads.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What does a reef cost a fishing family to gain?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: One family might see steadier catches once the structures settle, yet the study will show the real balance.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Mm.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Palabra BCS says Mayor Milena Quiroga will pay the MXN 71.5m year-end bonus early, from city revenue only.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: No loan for December wages.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: She moved the date to 12 November and used early property-tax money. Workers get the cash before the holidays. The 30% discount drew payments forward.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: How long can that revenue last when the sea keeps changing?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The early taxes helped this round, yet the city still watches its own income grow slowly.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The tide and the tax roll move together.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Tribuna de México notes CEA and CONAGUA will spend over MXN 400m on 134 water projects, including Loreto’s plant and four desal plants.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The desert asks for water before the budget answers.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The Palo Verde aqueduct and El Novillo studies sit inside those numbers, alongside the annual base of roughly 35m.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Who watches the first drop reach the pipes?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: HOY BCS adds the state sent Congress a MXN 28.3bn proposal for 2027, with own revenue rising to 14.6 percent.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Does the extra share reach the reefs and the pipes first?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Congress will decide in December. The plan lists education, health and public works ahead of tenders in January.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: A quiet choice that shapes the next swell.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Luz, the revenue numbers from Los Cabos keep coming back.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Gringo Gazette reports the 2027 law at 6,746 million pesos, down 9 percent. Own-source revenue drops almost 20 percent from property and transfer taxes.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: That cooling real estate market touches everything else. What does the desert teach the city when the light on the sales signs starts to fade?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: El Economista notes BBVA Research's IPAVIR index at 144.2 in BCS versus 83.6 nationally, driven by investment purchases that are now slowing.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Mm. And the tourism side feels it too.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Meganoticias has Senator Zatarain warning of 25 to 35 percent sales drops and at least 27 restaurants closed or paused.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The hidden thread runs through stalled projects as well.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Like the wastewater plant in San José. Meganoticias notes the purchase stuck over OOMSAPAS debts while the plant already treats double its design flow.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What about the money that never reaches the municipalities?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Tribuna de México reports Congress asking for full disclosure on Cabo San Lucas marina fees and revenue, then seeking a state concession so the funds stay local.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: But here's the thing. The portal's base de datos shows Los Cabos already receives over 1,282,611,261 pesos in revenue shares, yet the hidden infrastructure still depends on those same cooling taxes. And Gringo Gazette notes the new climate fund now waits for tourist-tax earmarks that may never arrive.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Did you know that in 2025 Baja California Sur recorded 8,993 housing finance actions worth 6,560 million pesos?

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Mm. That is a large sum. What does it look like on the ground?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Imagine one modest home in La Paz. The financing covers the walls, the pipes, the roof. Multiply that across thousands of families and you see the scale.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: And yet the same state lists 22 aquifers already in deficit. How does the money flow when the water does not?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The portal’s economy guide shows the housing numbers clearly. Meanwhile the municipal shares from Anexo I.33 give Los Cabos 1282611261 pesos and La Paz 837464432 pesos.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: So the finance is moving. The question is whether the desert will let the houses keep their promise.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Exactly. The numbers tell one story. The aquifers tell another. CONAGUA reported the combined deficit at 105.1 million cubic meters per year.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: A quiet tension under every new roof.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The portal’s visión sees a polycentric economy ahead.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Baja California Sur does not hold together toward 2050 as one coastal formula. Los Cabos stays the tourism engine under stress. La Paz becomes the services and water-energy node. Comondú holds room for agriculture. The north adds remote generation.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What happens if growth stays uneven?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Constant-price GDP reached 187,152 million pesos in 2024, up 3.5 percent from 2023, INEGI reports. FDI moved from 1,353 million USD in 2024 to 1,578 in 2025, CNIE data shows. Formal IMSS employment fell 1.1 percent year-on-year in October, with 224,460 posts in September.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: So the 3.5 percent goal and tripling FDI remain forum proposals.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Yes. The aspiration is a regenerative system where investment spreads. La Paz, Comondú and the north each keep distinct roles. New growth meets real water and energy margins first.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What would it take for those roles to stay distinct?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: East Cape and Loreto respect protected-area ceilings. Comondú and the north add production without emptying services elsewhere. The 2027 budget package of 28.3 billion pesos reaches Congress in December, with the public event set for 27 November in La Paz.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Mm. The watchlist starts there.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The takeaway is this. When Los Cabos projects a 9% revenue drop and the state proposes 28.3 billion pesos for next year, the old model shows its limits.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: One coastal engine cannot carry every payroll or every town.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: La Paz brings forward its 71.5 million peso year-end bonus without new borrowing. BBVA notes housing prices here diverge most from incomes.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: And the senator warns of restaurant closures if tourists stay away.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: A polycentric economy spreads the work. Investment reaches Loreto, Comondú and the interior instead of cloning the same coast. The state doubles dengue brigades and pledges support to Comondú and Mulegé.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Formal jobs then rest on more than tourism. Over 400 million pesos go to water works across the state.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Stay with us. More Radio BCS2050 after the music.
